newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close off highs in anxious trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close off highs in anxious trade.

text.p: A postponement in the imminent swearing in of P. Chidambaram as finance minister put a lid on enthusiastic buying as Delhi share prices closed a shade higher in mixed trade on Wednesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 2.62 points higher at 801.24. The index had surged 2.1 percent in early trade.

"Though the market sentiment remained bullish following the likely return of Chidambaram as finance minister, the postponement of swearing in ceremony had some adverse affect on the sentiment," said Sanjay Kaul of brokers Kaul and Company.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma will induct Chidambaram and new ministers into Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government on Thursday at 6 p.m. (1230 GMT), the president's spokesman said.
The swearing-in ceremony had initially been set for Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. (1400), but was delayed at the request of some of the prospective ministers.
Reliance Industries ended 3.95 rupees higher at 316.70 on buying by foreign funds, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 5.15 rupees to 319.75.

The Delhi Stock Exchange will remain closed on Thursday following protests by exchange officials and brokers against a breakdown of airconditioning facilities in the stock exchange building, bourse officials said.
